problem.text: What is the GCD of $15$ and $24$?

steps.title: Where to start: write both numbers as primes
steps.body: The GCD (greatest common divisor) is the largest number that divides both. The cleanest way to find it is to break each number into prime powers, because then you can compare them one prime at a time.

your_turn.prompt: Write $15$ and $24$ as products of primes.

steps.title: Take the smallest exponent of each prime
steps.body: List every prime that appears in either number: $2$, $3$ and $5$. For the GCD, use the smallest exponent of each prime. Careful: a prime that divides only one of the numbers has exponent $0$ in the other, so its smallest exponent is $0$.

your_turn.prompt: What exponent of $2$ goes into the GCD? What exponent of $5$?
your_turn.answer: Both are $0$: $15$ has no factor of $2$, and $24$ has no factor of $5$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The prime $3$ appears once in each number, so its smallest exponent is $1$.
$$\gcd(15, 24) = 2^0\cdot 3^1\cdot 5^0 = 3$$
The answer is **$3$**.
